label: A second, mirrored labelling clause that casts the narrator: after one clause casts someone as something (sees him as a hero, calls her a liar), a following clause casts me or us (and she sees me as a nuisance, they treat us as outsiders); it fires on the 'as' or 'a' right after 'me'/'us', whoever does the labelling and whether or not the label is handed back. The same second clause aimed at him, her, you or them is weak, as is a one-way label of me with no earlier labelling clause, or me labelled in the first clause and answering back. Strongest when a sentence of setting comes first.

probed_before.source: this checkout's .probe-log, before the pre-registration commit

qc.label_under_test: A label handed back between two people: one person labels another (sees him as a tyrant, calls him a bore, considers him reckless) and then that other person labels the first in return (and he sees me as a slacker); it fires on the returned label's opening ('me', 'as', 'a', 'like'), friendly or hostile labels alike, with or without a sentence introducing the pair. A plain tit-for-tat with no label (I hate him and he hates me), a one-way label, or two people labelling the same third party stays quiet, and it is weak when the narrator is labelled first and answers back.
